sources.scope_note: Chinese-language official educational description of attitude frames and the sensor-controller-actuator loop; not a normative terminology standard or a fault-specific diagnosis source.

sources.title: Basilisk Version 2.11.0 Release Notes
sources.scope_note: Release-specific compatibility and packaging record. It does not by itself establish a fault model, physical effect, or telemetry truth.

sources.title: NEOSSat: Operational and Scientific Evolution of Canada’s Resilient Space Telescope
sources.scope_note: Public operational history describing magnetometer, torque-rod controller and X reaction-wheel anomalies. Preserve explicit uncertainty: the 2021 X-wheel cause was suspected electrical, not confirmed.

sources.title: Fault modeling of general momentum exchange devices in spacecraft attitude control systems
sources.scope_note: Models reaction wheels and single-gimbal CMGs as motor/variable-speed-drive cascades. Model-specific additive/multiplicative fault results must not be generalized beyond stated assumptions.

sources.title: Fault detection and diagnosis in a spacecraft attitude determination system
sources.scope_note: Uses rate gyros and vector sensors with Kalman filtering and gyro-bias estimation; additive sensor-fault formulation is a model assumption, not a universal physical failure law.

sources.title: Advanced fault detection and diagnosis in spacecraft attitude control systems: Current state and challenges
sources.scope_note: Review of spacecraft attitude-control FDD methods and practical gaps including residual sensitivity, model fidelity, noise, tuning and robustness.

sources.title: IMAGE Failure Review Board Final Report
sources.scope_note: NASA FRB report. The board assessed an SEU-induced SSPC instant trip as the likely cause of transponder power loss; the device status telemetry could indicate closed while output was actually off. Battery short/open and solar-array short/open are analyzed as alternative hypotheses and explicitly not observed IMAGE anomalies.

sources.title: NOAA-13 Satellite Solar Array Bus Short to Ground
sources.scope_note: NASA Lessons Learned records a NOAA-13 in-orbit loss of solar-array-to-battery charging. The cause was surmised by the operations team and concluded by the GSFC FRB as a solar-array bus-to-ground short, possibly from thermal cycling causing mounting bolts to penetrate insulation. Preserve the source's surmised/likely status.

sources.title: Lessons Learned from IDEASSat: Design, Testing, on Orbit Operations, and Anomaly Analysis of a First University CubeSat Intended for Ionospheric Science
sources.scope_note: The paper's abstract and conclusions attribute the extended power-down/communications blackout to the EPS reset circuit's inability to recover from an ionizing-radiation-induced SEL. The single-gate CMOS Schmitt-trigger inverter is identified as the likely susceptible element. This is the authors' flight-data-based diagnosis; distinguish it from a direct measurement of the internal device current waveform.

sources.title: TERRA Battery Thermal Control Anomaly — Simulation and Corrective Actions
sources.scope_note: Reports an October 2009 battery cell voltage anomaly and simultaneous loss of several battery-heater control circuits. Primary and redundant heater-control sides both showed anomalous behavior. The paper develops a thermal model from telemetry; it does not establish that one anomaly caused the other.

sources.title: TDRS-8 Power Challenges and Planning for End of Mission
sources.scope_note: NASA engineering presentation reports six of 32 solar-array circuit failures, BVL modules shunting a static current rather than regulating, and four underperforming battery cells. It is an on-orbit condition report; it does not specify the internal root cause of each failed circuit/module.

sources.title: Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP) Battery Operations Problem Resolution Team
sources.scope_note: NESC report documents repeated NiH2 cell voltage collapses on orbit. A 1.4 V reduction is consistent with complete self-discharge of one cell; root cause was not definitively determined. Team consensus theory involved electrolyte bridging between two cell stacks within a common pressure vessel.

sources.title: Spacecraft electrical power subsystem: Failure behavior, reliability, and multi-state failure analyses
sources.scope_note: Statistical analysis of more than one thousand spacecraft launched 1990–2008. Useful for subsystem-level failure/reliability context across batteries, distribution and solar arrays; not a component-level causal case record.

sources.title: NASA State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology — 3.0 Power
sources.scope_note: NASA chapter on solar generation, battery energy storage, power management and distribution. It is architecture/technology reference material, not evidence that a specific flight fault occurred.

sources.title: Terra Spacecraft Anomalies — Hex Bay Battery Cell and Heater Control
sources.scope_note: NASA Terra status summary records BBAT cell #50 near-zero voltage and loss of cell pressure, four of nine heater groups losing temperature control, and a suspected common MMOD strike as the likely cause. Preserve 'likely/suspected'; the summary does not describe a recovered fragment or confirm the impact point.
